items.title: Brent falls below $89 to lowest since late August; OPEC+ meets 29 Nov on 2027 quotas
items.text: Brent fell below $89 on 23 November for the first time since late August; the January 2027 contract touched $86.20 intraday and settled provisionally at $86.58 per Investing.com, as cited by House of Saud. Business Recorder had Brent at $88.97 and WTI at $79.94 early on 24 November, citing rising Middle East flows, Libya's Sharara pipeline reopening, and Deutsche Bank's estimate of a 52 million barrel October global inventory build. OPEC+ meets in Vienna on 29 November to set 2027 quotas, with current authorisations expiring 31 December. Lower crude trims realisations for ONGC and Oil India, though it eases India's import bill and helps refiners and gas users.

items.title: India's October crude import bill jumps to $19.5 bn; April-October at $111 bn
items.text: India's crude import bill for October 2026 was $19.5 billion, up nearly 88% year-on-year, with volumes up only 11%, so price drove most of the rise. Provisional PPAC data put April-October crude imports at $111 billion (+53.5%) on volumes up 2.7% to 146.6 million tonnes. LNG imports cost $11 billion (+35.8%) on volumes up 7.4% to 22,175 MMSCM. A heavy import bill keeps pressure on the government to back domestic output, which supports ONGC and Oil India.

items.title: Brent settles at $92.57 on 20 Nov, third weekly fall; OPEC+ meets 29 Nov on 2027 quotas
items.text: Brent's January contract settled at $92.57 on 20 November, up 0.64% on the day but down 3.41% on the week from $95.84, its third straight weekly loss. WTI settled at $83.98. A tanker fire near Hormuz lifted prices on Friday, while the IEA's view that supply is back in surplus weighed on them. OPEC+ is expected to set 2027 production levels on 29 November. Lower crude trims upstream realisations for ONGC, Oil India and Reliance.

items.title: Brent heads for third weekly fall at about $91.31 as Hormuz flows return to pre-war levels
items.text: Brent was down 67 cents (0.7%) at $91.31 a barrel on 20 November and on track for a near 5% weekly decline; WTI was at $82.85, heading for a 6.5% weekly drop. Crude shipments through Hormuz have returned to roughly pre-war levels, raising surplus expectations, while Houthi threats and tanker incidents keep a risk premium. OPEC+ meets on 29 November to set 2027 output policy. Lower crude eases India's import bill but trims realisations for ONGC and Oil India.

items.title: Brent settles flat at $91.98 as Hormuz mine reports offset US stock build; WTI at $83.21
items.text: Brent settled up 3 cents at $91.98/bbl on 19 November and WTI eased 5 cents to $83.21, its lowest close since 26 August. Iran's navy said two tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz (unverified by Reuters), while a larger-than-expected US inventory build and a 21% rise in Saudi September crude exports (5.38 mb/d, JODI) weighed. The IEA put cumulative Middle East conflict losses at 2.8 billion barrels of oil and 60 bcm of Gulf gas. Lower crude pressures upstream realisations for ONGC and Oil India but eases the import bill and marketing margins for OMCs.

items.title: Brent near $93.09 as US crude stocks rise 5.3 mb and Goldman flags possible 2027 surplus
items.text: Brent traded at $93.09 a barrel, down 0.05%, after settling at $93.14 on 17 November, and has fallen about 20% in November (WTI down 16%). US crude inventories rose 5.3 million barrels last week, the IEA expects a surplus of about 2 million barrels per day this quarter, and Goldman Sachs reportedly warned of a possible surplus next year as Middle East exports recover. Hormuz attacks, including the IRGC's claim that four tankers struck mines, limit the downside. Lower crude would weigh on realisations for upstream producers, while helping refiners and gas buyers.

items.title: Iran claims three tankers hit mines in Hormuz; US disputes, says main routes are clear
items.text: Iran's navy and Revolutionary Guards said three tankers hit naval mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz on 13-14 November. No ship has been named, Reuters could not verify the claims, and the US military says it has cleared the main routes. Brent settled at $95.84 on 13 November, its second weekly loss, and futures reopened Sunday evening. Confirmation would be an upside risk for crude and for India's import bill. A rebuttal that holds would favour the downstream refiners over upstream producers such as ONGC and Oil India.

items.title: Brent settles at $95.84, second weekly fall; IEA sees Q4 surplus for first time since war began
items.text: Brent's January contract settled at $95.84/bbl on 13 November and WTI at $88.56, each down about 2.5% on the week after a roughly 13% drop the week before. The IEA's monthly report said the market returns to surplus this quarter for the first time since the Iran war began, with crude inventories up 1.7 million b/d in October, though supply stays tight and Hormuz tanker attacks continue. Lower crude trims upstream realisations for ONGC and Oil India but eases the import bill and refiner input costs.

items.title: Oil India Q2 consolidated profit up 53% to Rs 2,521 crore; Rs 7 interim dividend
items.text: Oil India's board on 12 November reported Q2 FY27 standalone PAT of Rs 2,259 crore (+116%) and consolidated PAT of Rs 2,521 crore (+53%). Crude output rose 20% to 1.021 MMT and the realised crude price was US$92.24/bbl, up 35% from US$68.19. An interim dividend of Rs 7 per share was recommended. Consolidated profit was down 37% from Rs 4,026.83 crore in the June quarter.

items.title: EIA November STEO: Brent near $100 to year-end, $97 in 2026, $86 in 2027
items.text: EIA's November outlook expects Brent near $100/bbl through end-2026, averaging $97 in 2026 and $86 in 2027, falling to $77 by Q4 2027. Brent averaged $124 in October and fell below $100 on 4 November. Middle East shut-ins averaged an estimated 2.5 million b/d in October, down from a 10.9 million b/d peak in May, and stock builds of 3.5 million b/d are projected for H1 2027. The 2027 price path is supportive for upstream earnings but implies lower realisations next year.

items.title: DGH extends OALP-X/XI deepwater bid deadline to 10 December, seventh extension for OALP-X
items.text: The deadline for deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks in OALP-X and OALP-XI moved from 15 November to 10 December 2026; DGH gave no reason. Industry sources link it to the Rs 84,084 crore Samundra Manthan offshore scheme (guidelines 22 October), which covers up to 50% of deepwater drilling costs, capped at Rs 675 crore per well. This is the seventh extension for OALP-X, so the 15 November closing date in the weekly edition is superseded.

items.title: ONGC Q2 standalone profit up 57.3% to Rs 15,489 crore; Rs 8 interim dividend
items.text: ONGC's standalone Q2 FY27 net profit rose 57.3% year-on-year to Rs 15,489 crore (down 9.1% on Q1); H1 profit was Rs 32,522 crore. Nominated-field crude realisation averaged $92.33/bbl, up 37.1%, but standalone crude output fell 4.2% to 4.437 MMT and total oil and gas output fell 2.9% to 9.515 MMT. The interim dividend is Rs 8 per share (record date 12 November), and two Western Offshore projects worth about Rs 11,800 crore were awarded. Higher realisations are lifting earnings while volumes still slip.

items.title: Brent settles at $104.77, down 7.6%, as Iran signals openness to peace talks
items.text: Brent settled at $104.77 a barrel on 2 November, down 7.6% from Friday's $113.43, and WTI fell 7.4% to $96.46, back below $100. The slide followed reports of Iran-Qatar contacts over the Strait of Hormuz and a statement by Iran's president that the Supreme Leader had given the government more authority to pursue peace talks. It reversed much of the war premium built in October, but the article notes the conflict has not ended. Lower crude would ease pressure on India's import bill and on refiners and gas distributors, while cutting realisations for producers such as ONGC and Oil India.

items.title: OPEC+ core-7 hold December output targets at September levels; full 21-member meeting on 29 Nov
items.text: Seven core OPEC+ members kept December required production at September levels, about 31 million bpd combined (Saudi Arabia 10.478 mb/d, Russia 9.949 mb/d). Most Gulf members are pumping below target because of the Iran war, so the hold adds no supply. All 21 members meet on 29 November to set 2027 quotas after a capacity review due by mid-November; Rystad's Jorge Leon called the 2027 call 'extremely difficult', and forecasters warn of a 2027 surplus if Gulf flows normalise. For India, Brent staying elevated supports ONGC, Oil India and Vedanta realisations but raises the import bill and downstream cost pressure.

items.text: The December Brent contract expired on 30 October at $117.64, up $2.76 (2.4%), after touching $118 intraday. UKMTO reported a tanker hit by explosives attached by a small boat in Hormuz, described by sources as the first known successful limpet-mine strike there since the war began in February. For India, crude near $113-118 supports ONGC and Oil India realisations but raises import-bill and refiner margin pressure.

items.title: Brent settles at $117.64, a six-month high, after Hormuz tanker mine attack; up 13.6% in October
items.text: Brent's expiring December contract settled at $117.64/bbl, up $2.76 (2.4%), after touching $118; the more active January contract settled at $113.43 and WTI at $104.12. The move followed what maritime sources called the first known limpet-mine strike on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz since the war began, and fears of escalation after the 3 November US midterms; Qatari mediation and a letter from Vance seeking to revive talks had no Iranian response yet. Brent rose 13.6% in October (WTI +15.2%), which supports upstream realisations for ONGC and Oil India but raises the import bill and under-recovery pressure on oil marketing companies.

items.text: Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree on 24 October listed Aramco facilities at Yanbu, the Rabigh refinery and the East-West Pipeline as targets, though Saudi Arabia has not confirmed damage to oil infrastructure. items.title: India raises petrol export duty to Rs 2.5/litre, cuts diesel to Rs 8.5 in fortnightly review
items.text: A Finance Ministry notification effective 16 October raised the export duty on petrol to Rs 2.5 per litre from Rs 0.5 and cut diesel to Rs 8.5 per litre from Rs 16. The levies are reviewed every fortnight and track international crude and product prices. The lower diesel duty improves export margins for refiners, notably Reliance, while the levy remains a policy overhang on export-oriented refining.

items.title: Brent settles at $104.72 on 9 Oct as Gulf of Mexico storm shut-ins offset Iran-talk relief
items.text: Brent futures settled at $104.72/bbl on Friday 9 October, up 44 cents (0.42%), and WTI at $91.85, up 36 cents (0.39%). Producers halted more than 70% of US Gulf crude output ahead of Hurricane Isaias, lifting prices after earlier losses driven by Trump's pledge not to attack Iran before the midterm elections and China's planned resumption of refined fuel exports. Crude holding above $100 keeps ONGC and Oil India realisations high but weighs on oil marketing companies' margins and India's import bill.
